sources.news_title: Mamdani Calls On NYC Property Owners To Ban ICE
sources.text:
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani writes on X:
More than 100 elected officials have joined me in calling on parking lot and garage owners across New York City: Don’t give ICE a place to operate. Don’t rent to them. Tell them they’re not welcome.
Last week, ICE agents shot Oscar Belgal in the neck in Marble Hill while his 5-year-old son sat in the car. They had been staging nearby in a private parking lot.
Our city laws keep ICE off public property. Now, we’re calling on private property owners to do the same. One garage on Morton Street already removed ICE vehicles after neighbors spoke out. Every owner has that power.
Earlier this week several top NYC officials called for boycotting Target for allowing ICE to frequently use their parking lot as a staging area.

sources.news_title: New York leaders urge parking lot owners to keep ICE off their properties
sources.text:
Overview:
Led by NYC Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani, more than 100 elected New York state officials urged parking garage and lot owners to deny access to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The call seeks to address a gap in the sanctuary city’s protections, which restrict use of city-owned properties by ICE agents, but not private facilities.
NEW YORK — Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani led more than 100 elected officials from across New York state in calling on parking garage and lot owners to bar U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) from using their properties for immigration enforcement operations.
“We are asking that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations,” read the letter to more than 1,000 parking facility owners and operators.
“Our neighbors should not live in fear that the parking lot down the block could become a staging ground for an operation that puts their communities at risk,” the officials said.
The call comes one week after ICE agents shot Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old father, in the neck during an operation in Marble Hill while his 5-year-old son was in the car, prompting several protests. ICE had reportedly been using a nearby private parking lot associated with a Target store to surveil and arrest people in the residential neighborhood. Local officials had raised concern that the lot allows federal agents to conduct their activities near homes and businesses.
Under the city’s sanctuary policies to safeguard immigrants, law enforcement agencies outside the five boroughs generally may not use city-owned property as a staging area, processing location or base of operations without a judicial warrant or a limited legal exception. The protections cover city-owned parking facilities as well as schools, shelters and hospitals.
Private parking facilities, however, fall outside those restrictions. The latest appeal seeks to address that gap by asking property owners to voluntarily refuse ICE. It is not a legal prohibition.
Earlier this week, elected officials called on Target and the company that co-owns the Marble Hill parking lot to prevent ICE from using the property. According to local news reports, Target said it did not have a formal agreement with ICE.
More than 3.1 million New Yorkers were born outside the United States. They make up 43% of the city’s workforce, according to the Mayor’s Office, working across restaurants, shops, construction sites, hospitals and small businesses.
City officials said fear of immigration enforcement discourages residents from driving to work, running errands or carrying out day-to-day activities, with consequences for families, neighborhoods and the local economy.
“Owners who refuse to take part in these federal civil immigration enforcement operations advance public safety by protecting their own staff and customers, as well as fellow New Yorkers beyond their lots and garages,” the letter said. “They also tell every immigrant New Yorker that they are treasured members of this community, [that] our City welcomes them with open arms.”
For New Yorkers seeking immigration legal assistance, the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs operates an Immigration Legal Support Hotline at 800-354-0365.

sources.news_title: Fox Fact-Checks Mamdani on ICE Shooting as MS NOW Enables Democrats
sources.text:
On Monday morning, Fox & Friends fact checked Mayor Zohran Mamdani for spreading misinformation about the ICE shooting of illegal alien Oscar Bergal in contrast with MS NOW which has boosted claims peddled by Democrats.
The group zeroed in on an interview MS NOW host Jacob Soboroff did with Mayor Mamdani on Sunday's Connect show in which the New York Democrat claimed that the NYPD was unable to hold Bergal for ICE because there was no warrant out on him. He further hinted that DHS claims about Bergal having a criminal history were probably not true. From Sunday, Mamdani asserted:
Fox Fact-Checks Mamdani on ICE Shooting as MS NOW Enables pic.twitter.com/3PeZdRtQsh
— Brad Wilmouth (@bradwilmouth) October 13, 2026
There is no warrant for Mr. Bergal in New York City, and when I brought that up to the secretary, the secretary went into the same kind of language that you've heard from the secretary since, which is implications of criminality on the basis of evidence that will likely never be released. And we are too old not to know that trusting ICE at their word is a fool's errand. What we see, as you said, is a rinse-and-repeat and attempt to justify the unjustifiable no matter where it occurs across this country.
Fill-in co-host Rachel Campos Duffy listed items from Bergal's criminal record and referred to reports that he has a history of using a machete to threaten neighbors:
Hey, guys, how about trusting the neighbors of this criminal who said he was terrorizing all the neighbors with a machete. I mean, this is insane. Look at this rap sheet. Let's put that back up. We've got his rap sheet here, you guys. ... Prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, multiple arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession. And he also has Trinitarios gang associations.
Co-host Lawrence Jones then called out MS NOW's Soboroff for not challenging any of Mamdani's claims:
Couple of things, fact checks for the mayor. He knows that if someone has a deportation order, there's no criminal warrants, right? It's a civil process. That doesn't mean that the federal government does not have authority to pick the person up. So him -- and that reporter not pushing back and say, "Mr. Mayor, there's no warrant necessary to pick people that are in this country illegally.
During Soboroff's interview, the MS NOW host notably gave cover to Democrats who claim New York is not a sanctuary state by noting that New York City honored 24 detainers in 2025. But he did not mention that, according to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, the state of New York has ignored more than 14,000 detainers since President Donald Trump took office. Here's Soboroff:
MS NOW Enables Democrats Spreading Misinfo About ICE Shooting pic.twitter.com/HBNdezGuWk
— Brad Wilmouth (@bradwilmouth) October 14, 2026
SOBOROFF: The thing is, the city of New York does still cooperate, if I understand correctly, in limited cases. Is that right? This morning, your office shared with me that there were 24 instances of the New York City department of corrections honoring detainers in 2025 -- 13 of them meaning handing people over to ICE in 2026. So is that accurate?
MAMDANI: That is accurate. It is the law in New York City that for more than 170 serious violent crimes, when a judge signs off on a warrant that there is that handover.
Similarly, when Governor Hochul appeared on Deadline: White House, fill-in host Alicia Menendez allowed her without challenge to claim that New York is not a sanctuary for criminals.
And several MS NOW shows -- including Morning Joe, Deadline: White House, and Connect -- played a clip of Mamdani making the preposterous claim that ICE agents "have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save." None of the anchors challenged the comments even though ICE deports thousands of immigrants who have committed homicides each year.
Host Stephanie Ruhle even went so far as to fact-check Mullin without fact-checking Democrats.

They zero in on him, they work undercover, Lawrence. No one knows better than you. In law enforcement, sometimes you have to be undercover, especially with a guy that's hard to grab, at which time...

MS NOW's Connect with Jacob Soboroff
October 11, 2026
10:01 a.m.
JACOB SOBOROFF: We start today with continued outrage in response to Donald Trump's reign of immigration terror in cities and towns across this country. Yesterday, for the third day in a row, hundreds of protesters again took to the streets of New York City, calling on ICE to leave New York. This, of course, is in response to the shooting of 28-year-old Oscar Bergal by a federal immigration officer in the Marble Hill neighborhood of New York on Thursday. Bergal's five-year-old son was in the car when shots rang out.
(...)
As New Yorkers and the entire country grapple with ICE's brazen and ongoing brutality, the Trump administration points to familiar talking points like justifying the shooting, claiming Bergal refused lawful orders, weaponized his vehicle, and put officers' lives in danger. We have heard it all before. And, like clockwork, DHS has cast blame on Bergal himself. In a press conference on Friday, Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin characterized him like this: "a criminal, a thug, a gangbanger. The outrage should be with him for endangering the five-year-old."
It all sounds so familiar. ICE shoots first, DHS scrambles to justify, to blame, to demonize. Later, in an impassioned statement on Thursday night, the mayor of New York City, Zohran Mamdani, renewed his calls for the complete removal of ICE from New York City. Listen.
MAYOR MAMDANI: We know that ice is rotten to its core. Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save.
(...)
SOBOROFF: Do you think that ICE agents broke the law, particularly about how or when a police officer can use deadly force in New York state?
MAYOR MAMDANI: I think that what they have shown time and again is that they view the law as a suggestion. There is a reason why the NYPD would not be shooting at a moving vehicle. There is a reason why law enforcement agents are supposed to wear identifiable information and uniforms. What you could see in that video and in the videos that have been released since is people, bystanders outside unsure as to what they were even seeing. Because in that imagery, it feels as if you're almost looking at a mass shooter as opposed to seeing someone who is purportedly representing a federal agency.
(...)
And what struck me is the secretary did not think that ICE agents had done anything wrong. The same language that you were quoting from of the press conference that came the day after, is the same language that's being used in private. And I made clear that here in New York City, it is not acceptable to be firing at a moving vehicle -- to be shooting at an individual for whom there is no warrant to be shooting at a car where there is a five-year-old. It is not acceptable for ICE to be operating in the manner that they do. And so often the language that they use to describe the people that they are trying to detain is language that might be better suited to describe who they are and what they are doing.
(...)
You're talking about agents who are opening fire in broad daylight. Again, we're talking around 4 p.m. on a Thursday. We're talking about people carrying their shopping bags, walking by a bodega, thinking they're on their way home. Then they hear shots ring out, and they don't even know whether this is from someone who is supposed to be a law enforcement agent, or just someone who is terrorizing the city. And, when it comes to ICE, there is no difference between those two things.
(...)
They view so many people across this country innately as being criminals just by virtue of how they look, where they live, what language that they speak. That is not how we run New York City. That is not who we are as New Yorkers.
SOBOROFF: What charges did they ask you to bring against Mr. Bergal?
MAYOR MAMDANI: That's the other thing. When they said they wanted us to take Mr. Bergal into custody, I asked, "On what warrant? We do not have a warrant for Mr. Bergal in New York City." And when I asked that question, he started to go into the same language that he used in the press conference language that we know they have used to describe so many across this country which then, upon any further review, falls apart at the first inspection.
(...)
SOBOROFF: Secretary Mullen was on television this morning. He continues to criticize both you and New York City's sanctuary policies. Let me show you what he said on -- on CNN just this morning when he was asked.
SECRETARY MARKWAYNE MULLIN, DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY: If people are really concerned about -- about the tactics that are being used, how about the state cooperates with us? These individuals I've talked about have detainers on them. Oscar had a detainer on them.
SOBOROFF: The thing is, the city of New York does still cooperate, if I understand correctly, in limited cases. Is that right? This morning, your office shared with me that there were 24 instances of the New York City department of corrections honoring detainers in 2025 -- 13 of them meaning handing people over to ICE in 2026. So is that accurate?
MAMDANI: That is accurate. It is the law in New York City that for more than 170 serious violent crimes, when a judge signs off on a warrant that there is that handover. But what we hear from the secretary time and again is to imply that all people in this city, if they are of an immigrant background, could be criminals. And that is something that we firmly reject. We follow the law in New York City. And I know that to the secretary the law is merely a suggestion when it comes to the actions of these ICE agents.

sources.text:
NEW YORK (AP) — Mayor Zohran Mamdani and top New York Democrats are calling on the owners of private parking lots to block federal immigration officers from using their properties as staging areas, days after immigration officers shot a man in the city.
In a Friday letter, Mamdani, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and dozens of state and local lawmakers told lot and garage owners that the city needs their “help at a critical juncture.”
“In solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and in our shared commitment to the City we love, we ask that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations,” the letter reads. “Make it known to ICE that it is not authorized to use your garages and lots.”
The plea came after immigration officers shot 28-year-old Dominican national Oscar Belgal during an arrest last week as he rode in a car with his young son. The shooting sparked protests and drew renewed attention to the federal government’s immigration crackdown .
The federal officers had been using a nearby private parking lot as a staging area before the shooting, according to Friday’s letter.
A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security slammed the letter in a statement that read: “Mayor Mamdani should be grateful to our brave law enforcement officers for cleaning up the streets of NYC since he won’t. Luckily, no terminated parking will stop ICE from deporting criminal illegal aliens to make New York safe again.”
Federal officials maintain the immigration officers believed their lives were in danger and opened fire only after Belgal smashed his car into two government vehicles and accelerated toward them.
New York City has previously barred outside law enforcement agencies such as DHS from setting up staging areas on city property unless they have a judicial warrant or qualify for certain “limited legal exceptions,” according to the letter. “But these laws govern City property, not the private lots and garages that you operate,” it adds.
Private businesses have at times found themselves in the middle of tense political fights over President Donald Trump’s administration’s immigration enforcement push.
In one instance, a Minnesota hotel that refused to let immigration officers stay there in January apologized after public criticism from DHS, saying the decision violated its internal policies. In another, protesters occupied the lobby of a Manhattan hotel they said was housing some immigration officers.

sources.text:
Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images
(New York, New York) – New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is asking private parking garage and lot owners to stop allowing federal immigration agents to use their properties for enforcement operations.
The mayor announced the effort Friday, October 16, with support from more than 100 elected officials across New York.
In a letter to parking operators, Mamdani urged businesses to deny Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) access to their facilities, including for temporary staging areas used before federal arrests.
The request follows last week’s shooting in Marble Hill, where an ICE agent shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal during an attempted arrest. Belgal’s 5-year-old son was inside the vehicle at the time.
According to the mayor’s office, federal agents had gathered at a privately owned parking lot near the shooting location before conducting their operation.
Mamdani argues that allowing ICE to operate from neighborhood businesses creates safety concerns for employees, customers and nearby residents.
New York City already limits the use of municipal property for federal civil immigration enforcement. However, those restrictions do not automatically apply to privately owned parking facilities.
The mayor is now encouraging businesses to voluntarily adopt similar restrictions, rather than pursuing a new citywide requirement.

sources.text:
NEW YORK (1010 WINS) — Mayor Zohran Mamdani led a coalition of more than 100 elected officials across New York State in issuing a letter to over 1,000 private parking garage and lot owners across the five boroughs, urging them to prohibit ICE from using their properties as staging grounds for enforcement operations.

The letter follows an incident in Marble Hill where ICE agents shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in the neck inside a vehicle containing his 5-year-old son, after reportedly staging operations out of a nearby private lot.
"Last week, ICE agents shot a father in the neck in Marble Hill while his 5-year-old son sat in the car," Mamdani said. "City law already bars ICE from using City property as a base of operations. Federal agents are turning to private parking lots, including a lot just blocks from where they shot Mr. Belgal. I am asking every garage and lot owner in this city to stop giving them that option. Do not rent your property to ICE. Do not lend it to them. Tell them they are not welcome."
Mamdani emphasized that private operators hold the authority to keep federal authorities off their premises and cited a recent incident where a garage on Morton Street in Manhattan removed ICE vehicles after local residents raised concerns. "You're talking about agents who are opening fire in broad daylight," Mamdani stated, noting that federal agents have repeatedly demonstrated a disregard for local community safety.
The joint letter instructs property owners to formally inform ICE that its agents are not authorized to use their facilities, warning that allowing federal enforcement access places property, employees, and customers at the center of operations that terrorize local communities.
Local laws and executive actions restrict ICE from using city-owned properties, schools, shelters, and hospitals as staging areas without a judicial warrant. Those prohibitions do not extend to private real estate, prompting the citywide push by elected leaders.

sources.news_title: After Marble Hill shooting, Mamdani urges parking lot owners to keep ICE out
sources.text:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani and over 100 city and state elected officials wrote a letter on Thursday, Oct. 15, urging private parking garage and lot owners to not rent, lend, or allow ICE to use their property for immigration enforcement.
The letter follows the Marble Hill shooting of Oscar Belgal by federal agents as his 5-year-old son sat in the backseat. Following several sightings of ICE in the area, a coalition of elected officials in the Bronx and Upper Manhattan had reached out to Target and its co-owner, Kingsbridge Associates, to confirm whether they had formal agreements with ICE.
A Target spokesperson previously told the Bronx Times that it does not have a formal agreement with the federal agency. Two days after the shooting, Kingsbridge Associates told the elected officials that they were not aware that ICE was using their parking lot.
The shooting sparked protests against ICE’s presence in New York. Mayor Mamdani deployed the Strategic Response Group, whose officers violently clashed with protesters, including incoming Upper Manhattan representative Darializa Avila Chevalier, who was shoved to the ground.
In their letter, the officials warned that private parking lots and garages could serve as staging grounds for federal immigration enforcement operations, even without formal agreements between property owners and ICE.
Nationwide, there have been several reports of ICE agents using private parking lots for enforcement. In Queens, agents used two bank parking lots, while in Manhattan, agents used a garage on Morton Street. The Morton Street garage removed ICE vehicles after neighbors raised concerns, according to the mayor’s office.
“City law already bars ICE from using City property as a base of operations. Federal agents are turning to private parking lots, including a lot just blocks from where they shot Mr. Belgal,” Mamdani said.
“I am asking every garage and lot owner in this city to stop giving them that option. Do not rent your property to ICE. Do not lend it to them. Tell them they are not welcome.”
The shooting has left the Marble Hill community in fear. Residents described fears of another ICE sweep, as well as concerns about further gun violence, noting that the shooting happened in broad daylight at a busy intersection between the Metro-North station and the subway.
“Each such use, whether part of a formal or informal arrangement or no arrangement at all, gives ICE a launching point for operations that have terrified and terrorized local communities, and risks placing your property, your employees and your customers at the center of that,” the letter said.
Elected officials also received reports of ICE agents operating out of the BJ’s Wholesale Club in Marble Hill. Councilmember Pierina Sanchez said she and other officials were exploring all options to restrict ICE’s presence in the city.
At an Oct. 9 rally, Sen. Gustavo Rivera questioned whether Kingsbridge Associates were truly aware or not that ICE agents had been able to operate out of the parking lot for months.
“If I was upstairs right now in this parking lot, and I put up-I don’t know-a car wash, how long do you think I’d last there?” Rivera asked at an Oct. 9 rally.
“You think I’d last long? No, I wouldn’t. But ICE did for months.”

sources.news_title: Mamdani and 100+ NY officials urge parking lot owners to ban ICE
sources.text:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani and more than 100 elected officials across New York state are calling on private parking lot owners and operators across the five boroughs to ban U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers from using their property.
Mamdani and the officials released a letter Friday morning asking owners of parking lots and garages in New York City not to rent, lend or otherwise make their property available to ICE as a staging ground for immigration enforcement, and to inform the agency it’s not welcome on their property.
“Make it known to ICE that it is not authorized to use your garages and lots,” the letter says.
The letter comes just over a week after ICE officers shot and wounded Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican immigrant, in Marble Hill, blocks away from a Target parking lot that local officials say ICE officers had been recently using as a staging ground.
Mamdani and the other signatories highlighted the shooting and nearby parking lot in their Friday morning letter. Several local elected officials, clergy members, and immigrant advocates also rallied outside the Target last week, calling on New Yorkers to boycott the company.
A Target spokesperson previously told Gothamist that the company has no agreement with any federal immigration office. A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said that ICE officers didn’t use the Target parking lot as a staging ground the day Belgal was shot.
However, the DHS spokesperson added that ICE officers are legally authorized to use public parking lots, which they said was a standard practice for law enforcement agencies across the country.
The letter's signatories also include New York state’s two senators, Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand; the U.S. House of Representatives Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries; and dozens of other state and local elected officials, including City Council Speaker Julie Menin and the vast majority of the City Council.
Parking lots and garage owners across the city and country who allow ICE to use their property have come under fire by immigration advocates in recent months.
The elected officials’ letter specifically calls out ICE using two bank parking lots on Northern Boulevard in Queens and a garage on Morton Street in Lower Manhattan, both sites where protests have erupted over ICE’s alleged use of the facilities.
“Each such use, whether part of a formal or informal arrangement or no arrangement at all, gives ICE a launching point for operations that have terrified and terrorized local communities, and risks placing your property, your employees, and your customers at the center of that,” the letter says.
In May, the owner of the Morton Street garage ended its parking contract with ICE after local immigration activists protested the agency’s presence at the site, Gothamist first reported.
“We are grateful for this action and invite every owner to follow this courageous example,” the letter says of the Morton Street garage.
Local immigration activists have also in recent weeks protested a parking lot in Tribeca where they claim ICE is parking its vehicles. And the Hudson River Park Trust, a publicly owned corporation overseen by the state and city, let its long-standing parking contract with DHS expire in June after the local news outlet Hell Gate reported on it, prompting public outcry.
City government has also “acted with urgency” over the last year to ensure that its property, including its parking lots and garages, aren’t used for federal civil immigration enforcement actions, in accordance with city sanctuary laws, according to the letter.

sources.text:
Mamdani, Schumer and others urge NYC private property owners not to let ICE use parking areas as staging grounds
Mayor Zohran Mamdani, U.S. Sen. Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and 100 other local officials are urging that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents be prohibited from staging operations in private parking lots and garages in New York City.
City law already prohibits ICE from operating on city property absent a judicial warrant, but that prohibition does not extend to private property. Mamdani and the other signatories to a letter sent Thursday to 1,000 property owners ask them to adopt a similar prohibition to the city's.
"We write to ask for your help at a critical juncture for our City: we are asking that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations," says the letter, which adds: "ICE is using private parking facilities across the City as staging grounds for its operations: from two bank parking lots on Northern Boulevard in Queens, to a garage on Morton Street in Manhattan. Each such use, whether part of a formal or informal arrangement or no arrangement at all, gives ICE a launching point for operations that have terrified and terrorized local communities, and risks placing your property, your employees, and your customers at the center of that."
The letter cites urgency catalyzed by ICE agents’ shooting last week of Oscar Belgal, a Dominican national who was wounded on the Manhattan-Bronx border while in the car with his 5-year-old.
Belgal, who was struck in the neck, said through his lawyers that the agents never identified themselves before charging at his vehicle, guns drawn, and smashing his window with the butt of a gun. He tried to drive away and agents shot at the car as he left. ICE says he tried to barrel toward the agents, an account not shown on surveillance video released by the NYPD.
"ICE officers had been utilizing a privately owned parking lot only a few blocks away to stage their operations," the letter states. "In solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and in our shared commitment to the City we love, we ask that you do not rent, lend, or otherwise make your property available to ICE as a staging area for its enforcement operations."
The letter, shared by Mamdani’s office, was also signed by U.S. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and more than 100 state legislators, City Council members and others.
An unnamed spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, emailed that detentions and deportations would not be stopped by any loss of parking access.
“Mayor Mamdani should be grateful to our brave law enforcement officers for cleaning up the streets of NYC since he won’t. Luckily, no terminated parking will stop ICE from deporting criminal illegal aliens to make New York safe again,” said the statement, which included mugshots of immigrants who allegedly committed crimes and are in the country unlawfully.
In New York and across the country, Target has come under criticism and has been subject to protest because ICE has used the company's parking lots to stage operations. Target says it has no agreements with ICE.
The letter does not specifically name Target or any other company.
Meanwhile, a federal judge in Brooklyn ruled that New York City’s police and other local government agencies cannot be conscripted into enforcing civil immigration law, dismissing a lawsuit by the Trump administration challenging city sanctuary city policies. The ruling echoed Trump court losses across the country.

“They also tell every immigrant New Yorker that they are treasured members of this community and that our City welcomes them with open arms. I hope you will stand with us,” the letter said.

Mamdani’s letter cited at least three other instances of ICE using private lots to stage its operations across the city.
“Each such use, whether part of a formal or informal arrangement or no arrangement at all, gives ICE a launching point for operations that have terrified and terrorized local communities,” the draft read, adding that such deals risk “placing your property, your employees, and your customers at the center of that.”
Mamdani explained the ways in which the Big Apple blocks ICE from using its property for staging enforcement operations — in line with the city’s sanctuary policies, which bar cooperation with federal immigration enforcement — and flat-out asked garage owners to fall in line.
“These laws govern City property, not the private lots and garages that you operate. That is why we need your help,” the draft reads.
Hizzoner framed the plea as coming from a position of “solidarity with immigrant New Yorkers and our shared commitment to the city we love,” adding that it came at “a critical juncture for our city.”
The letter went even further — pulling at heartstrings with reminders that “every day, your garages and lots serve the people who make New York City work,” and telling the owners: “thank you for the essential service that you provide to millions of New Yorkers and visitors each day.”

sources.news_title: Advocates Applaud Mayor Mamdani’s Call to Keep ICE out of Parking Lots, Call for Stronger Protections - NYC, Long Island, New York State | New York Immigration Coalition
sources.text:
New York, NY—Today, NYC Mayor Mamdani released a letter calling on private New York City garage and parking lot owners to prevent and block United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents from using their property as a staging area for their enforcement operations and terrorizing New Yorkers.
The letter comes amid increased calls from advocates and elected officials urging the Target location at the Shops in Marble Hill to end all cooperation with ICE. For months, agents have been spotted using the plaza’s parking lot as a staging area for ICE enforcement operations, including shortly before an ICE agent shot Oscar Belgal last week. This is an important step toward limiting ICE’s ability to operate in our neighborhoods. But asking private businesses to keep ICE out is not enough. Mayor Mamdani must take stronger action to stop ICE from operating in New York City, including ending any cooperation between the NYPD and federal immigration authorities that facilitates immigration enforcement.
Murad Awawdeh, President and CEO, New York Immigration Coalition:
“Our neighborhoods should be places where families can live, work, and go about their daily lives without fear of being targeted by ICE or worrying that their children will become collateral damage in an ICE operation. We applaud Mayor Mamdani for urging private garage and parking lot owners to end their complicity with ICE’s violent actions. While this is a step in the right direction, more decisive action is needed to ensure that federal immigration enforcement is not facilitated by the NYPD. Every New Yorker, including business owners, has a responsibility to protect the people who keep the city running. Last week’s shooting of Oscar Belgal is a devastating reminder that ICE’s presence in our neighborhoods puts lives at risk, spreads fear, and undermines the safety of every New Yorker.”
